root_cause.text: The i915 driver violated hardware specifications by programming Variable Refresh Rate timing registers before enabling the Transcoder DDI Function Control, causing machine check exceptions and system hangs on Ice Lake platforms.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings` call from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder` to `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable` and adds a `WARN_ON` check verifying `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE` is set, while the CVE description explicitly states "ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL" and cites BSpec 22243 requiring this order.

intent_record.intent_summary: Removes an incorrect VRR timing configuration call from the Haswell transcoder setup routine.
intent_record.what: Removed the function call intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state) from the hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder function.
intent_record.how: Prevents the application of Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) specific timing configurations during CPU transcoder initialization on Haswell hardware.

grouping_result.intent: Removes an incorrect VRR timing configuration call from the Haswell transcoder setup routine.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the context where VRR timing registers were incorrectly programmed before Transcoder DDI Function Control was enabled. The vulnerability occurs when Variable Refresh Rate timing configuration happens prior to proper transcoder initialization, causing machine check exceptions on Ice Lake platforms.
